_comment: Production gtfs realm. The render-realm init container substitutes the eight placeholders below before Keycloak imports this — Keycloak 26.4 does not expand them itself, it stores the literal string as the client secret. Each placeholder must have a matching env var on that container, or the init container fails the pod rather than importing a placeholder as somebody's credential. Note it also rejects any leftover placeholder, so do not write a dollar-brace sequence anywhere in this file, including in a comment like this one. Import is create-only: once the realm exists, edits here do nothing until the keycloak database is dropped.
_comment_idps: trustEmail is true on all three, and it is load-bearing rather than a convenience: cafe-car matches a person to a pending feed invite, and to an account-link candidate, ONLY on a verified address, so with trustEmail false first-broker-login stores emailVerified=false and a feed shared by email silently never reaches a brokered user. GitHub, Google and GitLab each release only an address they have themselves verified, which is exactly what trustEmail is for. This does NOT weaken account linking: firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias still points at Keycloak's stock chain (Review Profile -> Create User If Unique | Handle Existing Account -> Confirm link -> Verify by email or re-auth), so an existing account is linked only after the user confirms — trustEmail governs only whether the address arrives marked verified, not whether linking is silent. A broker that does not verify addresses must stay trustEmail false; turn on the realm's verifyEmail instead.
